anomalies.observed: The 3.3 V rail is drawn as two distinct global nets that are never joined. The LDO output (REG1 pin 1) and the INA219 VS pin (U9.4), the PCA9685 VDD (U14.28), both EEPROMs (U15.4 / U17.4), the FLASH VCC (U6.8), the BMI088/IIS2MDCTR/MPRLS/TMP100/GPS VDD pins, etc. all sit on the net "+3.3V" (Power, FCC Peripherals, NAVC Peripherals sheets). Meanwhile the two MCU supply pins (FCC2 VBAT/VDD/VDDA, NAVC2 VDD/VDDA), the I2C pull-up resistors, the VDDA/VREF filter inputs and the CH330 USB-UART bridges sit on a separate net "+3V3" (FCC, NAVC, Connections sheets). No wire, junction or shared label connects "+3.3V" to "+3V3" on any provided sheet, so the MCU/peripheral pull-up/USB domain has no regulator feeding it. Note the 5 V rail is named consistently as "+5V" everywhere, so this split is unique to the 3.3 V rail.
anomalies.expected: A single 3.3 V net. The specification states "3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs" and "3.3 V LDO ... produces 3V3 for 'MCUs and Sensors'", i.e. the regulator output, the MCU VDD/VDDA/VBAT pins and the sensor/peripheral VDD pins must all share one rail.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: REG1 LD39200PU33R OUT pin 1 net label "+3.3V"; U9 INA219 VS pin 4 "+3.3V"
FCC sheet: FCC2 STM32H753VITx VBAT/VDD/VDDA pins and decoupling / I2C pull-ups / VDDA filter all on "+3V3"
FCC Peripherals sheet: U14 PCA9685PW VDD pin 28 "+3.3V" (same subsystem as FCC2, which is "+3V3")
"3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs"

anomalies.impact: As drawn the +3V3 domain (both MCUs, their I2C pull-ups, the USB-UART bridges and the VDDA/VREF filters) is not connected to the 3.3 V regulator output, so the MCUs and those devices are unpowered and the board does not boot; conversely the sensors/EEPROM/FLASH/PCA9685 on +3.3V would be powered but communicate with dead MCUs.

parsed.summary: The schematic splits the 3.3 V supply into two unconnected global nets, "+3.3V" (regulator output, sensors, EEPROMs, FLASH, PCA9685, INA219) and "+3V3" (both MCUs, I2C pull-ups, USB bridges), whereas the specification requires a single 3V3 rail feeding the MCUs and all sensors; this leaves the MCU supply net floating and is the primary anomaly. (The 5 V rail is named consistently, and the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap is not reported.)
